title.zh: 卷一百〇四 列傳第五十四: 高仙芝 封常清 哥舒翰
title.en: Volume 104 Biographies 54: Gao Xianzhi, Feng Changqing, Ge Shuhan
title.raw: 卷一百〇四 列傳第五十四: 高仙芝 封常清 哥舒翰 Volume 104 Biographies 54: Gao Xianzhi, Feng Changqing, Ge Shuhan

sentences.zh: 高仙芝，本高麗人也。

translations.literal: Gao Xianzhi was originally a man of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xianzhi was ethnically Korean.

sentences.zh: 父舍雞，初從河西軍，累勞至四鎮十將、諸衛將軍。

translations.literal: His father Sheji had at first followed the Hexi army; through accumulated merit he rose to Ten Generals of the Four Garrisons and a General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheji had first served with the Hexi armies and, through long service, risen to command in the Four Garrisons and to a guard generalship.

sentences.zh: 仙芝美姿容，善騎射，勇決驍果。

translations.literal: Xianzhi had a fine appearance, was skilled in mounted archery, and was brave, resolute, fierce, and bold.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was handsome, an expert horseman and archer, and notably brave and fierce in battle.

sentences.zh: 少隨父至安西，以父有功授遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: In youth he followed his father to Anxi; because of his father's merits he was appointed Mobile Strike General.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he accompanied his father to Anxi, where he received the rank of Mobile Strike General on account of his father's achievements.

sentences.zh: 年二十餘即拜將軍，與父同班秩。

translations.literal: Before he was thirty he was already commissioned as a general, of the same grade as his father.
translations.idiomatic: By his mid-twenties he had already been made a general, holding the same rank as his father.

sentences.zh: 事節度使田仁琬、蓋嘉運，未甚任用，後夫蒙靈察累拔擢之。

translations.literal: He served under Military Commissioners Tian Renwan and Gai Jiayun without being much employed; later Fumeng Lingcha repeatedly promoted him.
translations.idiomatic: Under the commissioners Tian Renwan and Gai Jiayun he saw little employment, but Fumeng Lingcha later promoted him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 開元末，為安西副都護、四鎮都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he became Vice Protector-General of Anxi and Commander-in-Chief of the military forces of the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Kaiyuan period he was serving as deputy protector of Anxi and commander of all military forces in the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 小勃律國王為吐蕃所招，妻以公主，西北二十餘國皆為吐蕃所制，貢獻不通。

translations.literal: The king of Lesser Bolü had been won over by Tibet, which gave him a princess in marriage; more than twenty states to the northwest were all controlled by Tibet, and tribute no longer reached the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Lesser Bolü had been drawn into Tibet's orbit and given a Tibetan princess as wife; more than twenty kingdoms in the northwest had fallen under Tibetan control, and their tribute no longer reached the court.

sentences.zh: 後節度使田仁琬、蓋嘉運並靈察累討之，不捷，玄宗特敕仙芝以馬步萬人為行營節度使往討之。

translations.literal: Later the commissioners Tian Renwan, Gai Jiayun, and Lingcha in succession campaigned against them without success; Emperor Xuanzong specially ordered Xianzhi, with ten thousand horse and foot, to serve as Mobile-Camp Military Commissioner and go to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners Tian Renwan, Gai Jiayun, and Lingcha had campaigned against them in turn without success, so Emperor Xuanzong personally ordered Xianzhi, at the head of ten thousand cavalry and infantry, to serve as mobile-camp commissioner and lead the punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 時步軍皆有私馬，自安西行十五日至撥換城，又十餘日至握瑟德，又十餘日至疏勒，又二十餘日至蔥嶺守捉，又行二十餘日至播密川，又二十餘日至特勒滿川，即五識匿國也。

translations.literal: At that time the infantry all had private horses. From Anxi it was fifteen days' march to Bola City, then more than ten days to Wusede, then more than ten days to Shule, then more than twenty days to the Onion Range garrison, then another twenty-odd days to the Bomi River, then another twenty-odd days to the Teliman River—that is, the land of the Five Shihni kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: The infantry all rode private mounts. From Anxi they marched fifteen days to Bola, another ten-odd days to Wusede, another ten-odd days to Kashgar, another twenty-odd days to the Onion Range garrison, another twenty-odd days to the Bomi River, and another twenty-odd days to the Teliman River—the territory of the Five Shihni kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 仙芝乃分為三軍：使疏勒守捉使趙崇玭統三千騎趣吐蕃連雲堡，自北谷入；

translations.literal: Xianzhi then divided his forces into three armies: he sent the Shule garrison commander Zhao Chongpin with three thousand cavalry to strike the Tibetan fortress of Lianyunbao, entering by the northern valley;
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi divided his army into three columns: he sent the Kashgar garrison commander Zhao Chongpin with three thousand horsemen against the Tibetan stronghold at Lianyunbao by the northern valley;

sentences.zh: 使撥換守捉使賈崇瓘自赤佛堂路入；

translations.literal: he sent the Bola garrison commander Jia Chongguan in by the Red Buddha Hall route;
translations.idiomatic: he sent the Bola garrison commander Jia Chongguan in by the Red Buddha Hall road;

sentences.zh: 仙芝與中使邊令誠自護密國入，約七月十三日辰時會於吐蕃連雲堡。

translations.literal: Xianzhi and the palace envoy Bian Lingcheng entered from the Protectorate of Chimi, agreeing to meet at the Tibetan Lianyunbao at the chen hour on the thirteenth day of the seventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi and the palace envoy Bian Lingcheng entered from Chimi, with orders to rendezvous at Lianyunbao at the seventh hour on the thirteenth day of the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 堡中有兵千人，又城南十五里因山為柵，有兵八九千人。

translations.literal: In the fortress there were a thousand troops; fifteen li south of the city, exploiting the mountain terrain, a stockade had been built with eight or nine thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: The fortress held a thousand men, and fifteen li south of the city a mountain stockade had been built with eight or nine thousand more.

sentences.zh: 城下有婆勒川，水漲不可渡。

translations.literal: Below the city was the Bole River; the water had risen and could not be crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Below the fortress lay the Bole River, swollen and impassable.

sentences.zh: 仙芝以三牲祭河，命諸將選兵馬，人賫三日幹糧，早集河次。

translations.literal: Xianzhi offered the three sacrificial animals to the river and ordered the generals to select troops and horses; each man was to carry three days' dry rations and assemble early at the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi sacrificed to the river and ordered his commanders to pick their men and mounts; each soldier was to carry three days' rations and report to the river at dawn.

sentences.zh: 水既難渡，將士皆以為狂。

translations.literal: Since the water was so hard to cross, officers and men all thought him mad.
translations.idiomatic: With the river so high, the troops all thought him mad to attempt a crossing.

sentences.zh: 既至，人不濕旗，馬不濕韉，已濟而成列矣。

translations.literal: When they arrived, men's flags were not wet, horses' saddles were not wet—they had already crossed and were formed up in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the far bank, not a flag was wet and not a saddle was soaked—they had crossed and were already drawn up in formation.

sentences.zh: 仙芝喜謂令誠曰：「向吾半渡賊來，吾屬敗矣，今既濟成列，是天以此賊賜我也。」

translations.literal: Xianzhi said delightedly to Lingcheng: "If the enemy had come upon us halfway across, we would have been defeated; now that we have crossed and are formed up, Heaven is giving me these bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi said happily to Lingcheng, "Had the enemy struck while we were midstream, we would have been ruined. Now that we are across and in formation, Heaven has delivered these foes into my hands.

sentences.zh: 遂登山挑擊，從辰至巳，大破之。

translations.literal: He then climbed the mountain and attacked; from the chen hour to the si hour he inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He then stormed the heights and attacked; from the seventh hour until the ninth he routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 至夜奔逐，殺五千人，生擒千人，餘並走散。

translations.literal: He pursued through the night, killing five thousand men, capturing a thousand alive; the rest all fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued through the night, killing five thousand and taking a thousand prisoners; the rest fled in all directions.

sentences.zh: 得馬千餘匹，軍資器械不可勝數。

translations.literal: He obtained more than a thousand horses; military supplies and weapons were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He seized more than a thousand horses and booty in arms and supplies beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 玄宗使術士韓履冰往視日，懼不欲行，邊令誠亦懼。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong had the diviner Han Lübing go to observe the sun; he was afraid and did not wish to go, and Bian Lingcheng was also afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had sent the diviner Han Lübing to observe the heavens; Han was afraid to proceed, and Bian Lingcheng was afraid as well.

sentences.zh: 仙芝留令誠等以羸病尪弱三千餘人守其城，仙芝遂進。

translations.literal: Xianzhi left Lingcheng and others with more than three thousand sick, weak, and feeble men to hold the fortress, and Xianzhi then advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi left Lingcheng behind with more than three thousand sick and weak troops to hold the fortress and pressed on.

sentences.zh: 三日，至坦駒嶺，直下峭峻四十餘里，仙芝料之曰：「阿弩越胡若速迎，即是好心。」

translations.literal: On the third day they reached Tanju Ridge and descended straight down a precipice of more than forty li. Xianzhi judged and said: "If the Anüyue barbarians come quickly to meet us, that shows good will.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day they reached Tanju Ridge and descended a sheer cliff of more than forty li. Xianzhi reasoned aloud, "If the Anüyue tribesmen hurry to greet us, their hearts are with us.

sentences.zh: 又恐兵士不下，乃先令二十餘騎詐作阿弩越城胡服上嶺來迎。

translations.literal: He also feared the soldiers would not descend, so he first sent more than twenty horsemen disguised in Anüyue city barbarian dress up the ridge to come and welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing his men would refuse to go down, he first sent twenty-odd horsemen disguised as Anüyue tribesmen up the ridge to welcome the army.

sentences.zh: 既至坦駒嶺，兵士果不肯下，云：「大使將我欲何處去？」

translations.literal: When they reached Tanju Ridge, the soldiers indeed refused to go down, saying: "Commissioner, where are you taking us?
translations.idiomatic: At Tanju Ridge the troops indeed refused to descend, crying, "Commissioner, where are you leading us?

sentences.zh: 言未畢，其先使二十人來迎，云：「阿弩越城胡並好心奉迎，娑夷河藤橋已斫訖。」

translations.literal: Before they had finished speaking, the twenty men he had sent ahead came to welcome them, saying: "The Anüyue city barbarians are all of good will in receiving you; the vine bridge over the Suoyi River has already been cut down."
translations.idiomatic: Before they had finished, the twenty advance riders appeared, calling out, "The Anüyue tribes welcome you in good faith—the vine bridge over the Suoyi River has already been cut!"

sentences.zh: 仙芝陽喜以號令，兵士盡下。

translations.literal: Xianzhi feigned delight in his orders, and the soldiers all went down.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi pretended delight and gave the order; the men all went down.

sentences.zh: 娑夷河，即古之弱水也，不勝草芥毛發。

translations.literal: The Suoyi River is the ancient Weak Water; it cannot bear even a blade of grass or a hair.
translations.idiomatic: The Suoyi River was the ancient Weak Water, so light that not a blade of grass or a hair could float upon it.

sentences.zh: 下嶺三日，越胡果來迎。

translations.literal: Three days after descending the ridge, the Yue barbarians indeed came to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after they came down from the ridge, the Yue tribesmen did indeed come to greet them.

sentences.zh: 明日，至阿弩越城，當日令將軍席元慶、賀婁餘潤先修橋路。

translations.literal: The next day they reached Anüyue City; that same day he ordered Generals Xi Yuanqing and Helou Yurun to repair the bridge and road first.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they reached Anüyue City, and that same day he sent Generals Xi Yuanqing and Helou Yurun ahead to repair the bridge and road.

sentences.zh: 仙芝明日進軍，又令元慶以一千騎先謂小勃律王曰：「不取汝城，亦不斫汝橋，但借汝路過，向大勃律去。」

translations.literal: The next day Xianzhi advanced his army and again ordered Yuanqing with a thousand cavalry to go ahead and tell the king of Lesser Bolü: "We will not take your city or cut your bridge—we only ask to borrow your road to pass through toward Greater Bolü.
translations.idiomatic: The following day Xianzhi marched on and sent Yuanqing ahead with a thousand horsemen to tell the king of Lesser Bolü, "We do not mean to take your city or destroy your bridge—we only ask passage on our way to Greater Bolü.

sentences.zh: 城中有首領五六人，皆赤心為吐蕃。

translations.literal: In the city were five or six chieftains, all wholeheartedly serving Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Five or six chieftains in the city were utterly loyal to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 仙芝先約元慶云：「軍到，首領百姓必走入山谷，招呼取以敕命賜彩物等，首領至，齊縛之以待我。」

translations.literal: Xianzhi had first agreed with Yuanqing: "When the army arrives, the chieftains and common people will surely flee into the valleys—summon them with imperial orders and gifts of colored goods; when the chieftains come, bind them all together and wait for me.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi had briefed Yuanqing beforehand: "When our army arrives, the chieftains and populace will flee into the hills—call them back with imperial gifts; when the chieftains appear, bind them all and hold them for me.

sentences.zh: 元慶既至，一如仙芝之所教，縛諸首領。

translations.literal: When Yuanqing arrived, he did exactly as Xianzhi had instructed and bound all the chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing did exactly as instructed and seized every chieftain.

sentences.zh: 王及公主走入石窟，取不可得。

translations.literal: The king and the princess fled into a stone cave and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The king and princess had fled into a cave and could not be captured.

sentences.zh: 仙芝至，斬其為吐蕃者五六人。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi arrived, he beheaded the five or six who had served Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi arrived, he executed the five or six Tibetan loyalists.

sentences.zh: 急令元慶斫藤橋，去勃律猶六十里，及暮，才斫了，吐蕃兵馬大至，已無及矣。

translations.literal: He urgently ordered Yuanqing to cut the vine bridge; Bolü was still sixty li away, and by evening it was only just cut when Tibetan troops and horses arrived in force—it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently ordered Yuanqing to destroy the vine bridge. Bolü was still sixty li distant; by dusk the bridge was only just cut when a great Tibetan force arrived—too late to cross.

sentences.zh: 藤橋闊一箭道，修之一年方成。

translations.literal: The vine bridge was as wide as an arrow's flight; it took a year to complete its construction.
translations.idiomatic: The vine bridge spanned no more than an arrow's shot and had taken a full year to build.

sentences.zh: 勃律先為吐蕃所詐借路，遂成此橋。

translations.literal: Bolü had earlier been tricked by Tibet into lending a road, and thus this bridge was built.
translations.idiomatic: Bolü had earlier been tricked by Tibet into granting passage, which was how the bridge had been built.

sentences.zh: 至是，仙芝徐自招諭勃律及公主出降，並平其國。

translations.literal: At this point Xianzhi gradually persuaded Bolü and the princess to come out and surrender, and pacified their state.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xianzhi gradually persuaded the king of Bolü and the princess to surrender and pacified the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 天寶六載八月，仙芝虜勃律王及公主趣赤佛堂路班師。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year of Tianbao, Xianzhi took captive the king of Bolü and the princess and withdrew his army by the Red Buddha Hall route.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tianbao 6, Xianzhi took the king of Bolü and his princess captive and withdrew by the Red Buddha Hall road.

sentences.zh: 九月，復至婆勒川連雲堡，與邊令誠等相見。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he again reached Lianyunbao on the Bole River and met Bian Lingcheng and the others.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he returned to Lianyunbao on the Bole River and rejoined Bian Lingcheng and the rest.

sentences.zh: 其月末，還播密川，令劉單草告捷書，遣中使判官王廷芳告捷。

translations.literal: At the end of that month he returned to the Bomi River, had Liu Dan draft the victory report, and sent the palace envoy and judge Wang Tingfang to announce the victory.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end he returned to the Bomi River, had Liu Dan draft the victory dispatch, and sent the palace envoy Wang Tingfang to report the triumph to court.

sentences.zh: 仙芝軍還至河西，夫蒙靈察都不使人迎勞，罵仙芝曰：「啖狗腸高麗奴！

translations.literal: When Xianzhi's army returned to Hexi, Fumeng Lingcha sent no one from the capital to welcome or comfort them, and cursed Xianzhi, saying: "Dog-gut-eating Korean slave!
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi's army reached Hexi, Fumeng Lingcha sent no envoy from the capital to welcome them and cursed him: "Korean cur who eats dog guts!

sentences.zh: 啖狗屎高麗奴！

translations.literal: Dog-dung-eating Korean slave!
translations.idiomatic: Korean cur who eats dog shit!

sentences.zh: 於闐使誰與汝奏得？」

translations.literal: Who obtained your Khotan commission for you?
translations.idiomatic: Who got you your posting as commissioner of Khotan?

sentences.zh: 仙芝曰：「中丞。」

translations.literal: Xianzhi said: "The vice commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi replied, "You did, Vice Commissioner."

sentences.zh: 「焉耆鎮守使誰邊得？」

translations.literal: Who obtained the Yanqi garrison commandership for you?"
translations.idiomatic: And who secured you the Yanqi garrison command?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「中丞。」

translations.literal: He said: "The vice commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "You did, Vice Commissioner."

sentences.zh: 「安西副都護使誰邊得？」

translations.literal: Who obtained the Anxi deputy protectorship for you?"
translations.idiomatic: And who got you the deputy protectorship of Anxi?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「中丞。」

translations.literal: He said: "The vice commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "You did, Vice Commissioner."

sentences.zh: 「安西都知兵馬使誰邊得？」

translations.literal: Who obtained the Anxi command of all military forces for you?"
translations.idiomatic: And who made you commander of all Anxi forces?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「中丞。」

translations.literal: He said: "The vice commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "You did, Vice Commissioner."

sentences.zh: 靈察曰：「此既皆我所奏，安得不待我處分懸奏捷書！

translations.literal: Lingcha said: "Since I recommended you for all of these, how could you not wait for my disposition before submitting the victory report on your own!
translations.idiomatic: Lingcha said, "I recommended you for every one of these posts—how dare you send in a victory report without waiting for my approval!

sentences.zh: 據高麗奴此罪，合當斬，但緣新立大功，不欲處置。」

translations.literal: On this offense the Korean slave deserves execution, but because he has just won a great merit, I do not wish to punish him."
translations.idiomatic: For this offense the Korean wretch deserves death, but since he has just won a great victory, I will let it pass."

sentences.zh: 又謂劉單曰：「聞爾能作捷書。」

translations.literal: He also said to Liu Dan: "I hear you can write victory reports."
translations.idiomatic: He also told Liu Dan, "I hear you are skilled at drafting victory dispatches."

sentences.zh: 單恐懼請罪。

translations.literal: Dan, in fear, begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan, terrified, pleaded for mercy.

sentences.zh: 令誠具奏其狀曰：「仙芝立奇功，今將憂死。」

translations.literal: Lingcheng submitted a full report of the situation, saying: "Xianzhi has won a singular merit, yet now faces death in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Lingcheng reported the whole affair to court: "Xianzhi has achieved a remarkable victory, yet now fears for his life.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，制授仙芝鴻臚卿、攝御史中丞，代夫蒙靈察為四鎮節度使，征靈察入朝。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year an edict appointed Xianzhi Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting Censor-in-Chief, replacing Fumeng Lingcha as Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons and summoning Lingcha to court.
translations.idiomatic: That sixth month an edict made Xianzhi Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting censor-in-chief, replaced Fumeng Lingcha as commissioner of the Four Garrisons, and recalled Lingcha to the capital.

sentences.zh: 靈察大懼，仙芝每日見之，趨走如故，靈察益不自安。

translations.literal: Lingcha was greatly afraid; Xianzhi saw him every day and hurried to and fro as before, and Lingcha grew ever more ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Lingcha was terrified. Xianzhi still called on him daily and behaved deferentially as before, which only made Lingcha more uneasy.

sentences.zh: 將軍程千里時為副都護，大將軍畢思琛為靈察押衙，行官王滔、康懷順、陳奉忠等，嘗構譖仙芝於靈察。

translations.literal: General Cheng Qianli was then deputy protector; Grand General Bi Sichen was Lingcha's yaya; staff officers Wang Tao, Kang Huaishun, Chen Fengzhong, and others had once fabricated slanders against Xianzhi before Lingcha.
translations.idiomatic: General Cheng Qianli was deputy protector; Grand General Bi Sichen served as Lingcha's personal adjutant; and staff officers Wang Tao, Kang Huaishun, and Chen Fengzhong had once slandered Xianzhi to Lingcha.

sentences.zh: 仙芝既領節度事，謂程千里曰：「公面似男兒，心如婦人，何也？」

translations.literal: Once Xianzhi had taken charge of the commissioner's affairs, he said to Cheng Qianli: "Your face is like a man's, but your heart is like a woman's—why?
translations.idiomatic: After taking command, Xianzhi said to Cheng Qianli, "You look like a man, but your heart is that of a woman—why is that?

sentences.zh: 又謂思琛曰：「此胡敢來！

translations.literal: He also said to Sichen: "This barbarian dares to come!
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Bi Sichen, "How dare this barbarian show his face here!

sentences.zh: 我城東一千石種子莊被汝將去，憶之乎？」

translations.literal: My thousand-shi seed estate east of the city was taken away by you—do you remember?"
translations.idiomatic: You carried off my thousand-shi seed estate east of the city—do you remember that?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此是中丞知思琛辛苦見乞。」

translations.literal: He replied: "The vice commissioner knew how hard Sichen had worked and granted it upon my begging."
translations.idiomatic: Sichen replied, "The vice commissioner knew how hard I had worked and gave it to me when I begged for it."

sentences.zh: 仙芝曰：「吾此時懼汝作威福，豈是憐汝與之！

translations.literal: Xianzhi said: "At that time I feared you would abuse your power—how was that pitying you and giving it to you!
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi said, "At the time I was afraid you would abuse your authority—that was not pity for you!

sentences.zh: 我欲不言，恐汝懷憂，言了無事矣。」

translations.literal: I wanted not to speak, fearing you would brood over it; now that I have spoken, there is no further trouble."
translations.idiomatic: I had kept silent lest you worry; now that I have said it, there is nothing more to it."

sentences.zh: 又呼王滔等至，捽下將笞，良久皆釋之，由是軍情不懼。

translations.literal: He also summoned Wang Tao and the others, threw them down and was about to flog them, but after a long while released them all; from this the army's morale was unafraid.
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned Wang Tao and the others, threw them down for a beating, then after a long while released them all; from then on the troops had nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 八載，入朝，加特進，兼左金吾衛大將軍同正員，仍與一子五品官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he came to court, was given the special advancement rank, and concurrently made full Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard, with one son granted a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he came to court, was granted special advancement, and was made full grand general of the Left Golden Crow Guard, with one son given a fifth-rank post.

sentences.zh: 九載，將兵討石國，平之，獲其國王以歸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he led troops to attack the Stone Kingdom, pacified it, and brought back its king captive.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he led an expedition against the Stone Kingdom, conquered it, and brought its king back as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 仙芝性貪，獲石國大塊瑟瑟十餘石、真金五六馲駝、名馬寶玉稱是。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was greedy by nature; from the Stone Kingdom he obtained more than ten large stones of kingfisher feathers, five or six camels' loads of pure gold, and famous horses and precious jades in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was greedy by nature; from the Stone Kingdom he took more than ten large blocks of kingfisher jade, five or six camels' loads of pure gold, and famous horses and precious jades beyond count.

sentences.zh: 初，舍雞以仙芝為懦緩，恐其不能自存，至是立功，家財鉅萬，頗能散施，人有所求，言無不應。

translations.literal: At first Sheji had regarded Xianzhi as timid and slow, fearing he could not support himself; now that he had won merit, his household wealth ran to tens of thousands and he could give generously—when anyone asked something of him, he never refused to speak.
translations.idiomatic: At first Sheji had thought Xianzhi too timid to make his own way; now, after his victories, the family fortune ran to vast sums and he gave freely—whatever anyone asked, he never refused.

sentences.zh: 其載，入朝，拜開府儀同三司，尋除武威太守、河西節度使，代安思順。

translations.literal: That year he came to court, was appointed Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Bells and Tripod, and soon after removed as Administrator of Wuwei and Military Commissioner of Hexi, replacing An Sishun.
translations.idiomatic: That year he came to court and was made Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Bells and Tripod, then soon appointed administrator of Wuwei and military commissioner of Hexi in place of An Sishun.

sentences.zh: 思順諷群胡割耳捴面請留，監察御史裴周南奏之，制復留思順，以仙芝為右羽林大將軍。

translations.literal: Sishun incited the various Hu to cut their ears and twist their faces in petition to keep him; Censor Pei Zhounan memorialized this, and an edict kept Sishun in place while making Xianzhi Grand General of the Right Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Sishun stirred the frontier tribes to mutilate themselves in petition that he remain; Censor Pei Zhounan reported this, and the court kept Sishun in post while appointing Xianzhi grand general of the Right Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 十四載，封密雲郡公。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Miyun Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Miyun.

sentences.zh: 十一月，安祿山據范陽叛。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month An Lushan rebelled, holding Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month An Lushan rose in rebellion from his base at Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 是日，以京兆牧、榮王琬為討賊元帥，仙芝為副。

translations.literal: That same day the Metropolitan Governor and Prince of Rong, Li Wan, was made supreme commander for suppressing the rebels, with Xianzhi as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Prince Wan of Rong, who was also metropolitan governor, was named supreme commander against the rebels, with Xianzhi as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 命仙芝領飛騎、彍騎及朔方、河西、隴右應赴京兵馬，並召募關輔五萬人，繼封常清出潼關進討，仍以仙芝兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was ordered to lead the Flying Cavalry, the Crossbow Cavalry, and the troops of Shuofang, Hexi, and Longyou who were to hurry to the capital, and also to recruit fifty thousand men from the Guanfu region; following Feng Changqing he was to advance from Tong Pass to attack, and Xianzhi was also made concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was ordered to command the flying and crossbow cavalry and the Shuofang, Hexi, and Longyou forces rushing to the capital, to recruit fifty thousand men from the Guanzhong region, and to follow Feng Changqing through Tong Pass on the offensive; he was also made concurrent censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十二月，師發，玄宗禦望春亭慰勞遣之，仍令監門將軍邊令誠監其軍，屯於陜州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the army set out; Emperor Xuanzong went in person to Wangchun Pavilion to comfort and send them off, and again ordered Gate Guard General Bian Lingcheng to supervise the army, which encamped at Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the army marched. Emperor Xuanzong came in person to Wangchun Pavilion to see them off and again appointed Gate Guard General Bian Lingcheng to supervise the force, which encamped at Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 是月十一日，封常清兵敗於汜水。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of that month Feng Changqing's army was defeated at Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh of that month Feng Changqing was defeated at Sishui.

sentences.zh: 十三日，祿山陷東京，常清以餘眾奔陜州，謂仙芝曰：「累日血戰，賊鋒不可當。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day Lushan took the Eastern Capital; Changqing fled with his remaining troops to Shaan Prefecture and said to Xianzhi: "For days we have fought bloody battles—the rebels' momentum cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth Lushan captured the Eastern Capital. Changqing fled with his survivors to Shaanzhou and told Xianzhi, "After days of bloody fighting, the rebel onslaught cannot be stopped.

sentences.zh: 且潼關無兵，若狂寇奔突，則京師危矣。

translations.literal: Moreover Tong Pass has no troops; if the mad bandits burst through in a rush, the capital will be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Pass is undefended; if the rebels break through in a rush, the capital will be lost.

sentences.zh: 宜棄此守，急保潼關。」

translations.literal: We should abandon this defense and hurry to secure Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: We should abandon this position and rush to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 常清、仙芝乃率見兵取太原倉錢絹，分給將士，餘皆焚之。

translations.literal: Changqing and Xianzhi then led the troops at hand to take the money and silk from the Taiyuan granary, distributed them among the officers and men, and burned the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing and Xianzhi then led their remaining forces to seize the money and silk in the Taiyuan depot, distributed it among the troops, and burned what was left.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊騎繼至，諸軍惶駭，棄甲而走，無復隊伍。

translations.literal: Soon rebel cavalry followed; the armies were terrified, cast off their armor and fled, and no longer kept formation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebel cavalry caught up; the troops panicked, threw away their armor, and fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 仙芝至關，繕修守具，又令索承光守善和戍。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi reached the pass, he repaired the defensive equipment and also ordered Suo Chengguang to hold the Shanhe garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi reached the pass, he repaired the defenses and posted Suo Chengguang at the Shanhe garrison.

sentences.zh: 賊騎至關，已有備矣，不能攻而去，仙芝之力也。

translations.literal: When rebel cavalry reached the pass, preparations were already complete; they could not attack and withdrew—this was Xianzhi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel horsemen reached the pass, the defenses were ready; unable to attack, they withdrew—thanks to Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 封常清，蒲州猗氏人也。

translations.literal: Feng Changqing was a native of Yishi in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Changqing was a native of Yishi in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 外祖犯罪流安西效力，守胡城南門，頗讀書，每坐常清於城門樓上，教其讀書，多所歷覽。

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather, having committed a crime, was banished to Anxi to serve in labor; he guarded the southern gate of the barbarian city, read considerably, and each day seated Changqing on the gate tower and taught him to read, so that he perused many works.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandfather, convicted of a crime, had been exiled to Anxi for penal service and guarded the southern gate of a frontier town. A man of some learning, he would seat young Changqing on the gate tower each day and teach him to read, and the boy read widely.

sentences.zh: 外祖死，常清孤貧，年三十餘，屬夫蒙靈察為四鎮節度使，將軍高仙芝為都知兵馬使，頗有材能，每出軍，奏傔從三十餘人，衣服鮮明。

translations.literal: After his grandfather died, Changqing was orphaned and poor; past thirty, it happened that Fumeng Lingcha was Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons and General Gao Xianzhi was commander of all forces—quite talented; whenever he went on campaign he memorialized for more than thirty retainers, all in bright clothing.
translations.idiomatic: After his grandfather died, Changqing was left poor and alone. Past thirty, Fumeng Lingcha was commissioner of the Four Garrisons and General Gao Xianzhi commanded all forces—a capable officer who, on every campaign, petitioned for more than thirty retainers in splendid dress.

sentences.zh: 常清慨然發憤，投牒請預一傔。

translations.literal: Changqing, stirred with indignation, submitted a petition asking to be included among the retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing, indignant, submitted a petition asking to serve as one of the retainers.

sentences.zh: 常清細瘦目類腳短而跛，仙芝見其貌寢，不納。

translations.literal: Changqing was slight and thin, with eyes set close together, short-legged and lame; Xianzhi saw his appearance was poor and did not accept him.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing was slight, thin, close-set of eye, short-legged, and lame; Xianzhi took one look at his unprepossessing appearance and refused him.

sentences.zh: 明日又投牒，仙芝謂曰：「吾奏傔已足，何煩復來！」

translations.literal: The next day he submitted another petition; Xianzhi said to him: "My memorialized retainers are already sufficient—why trouble yourself to come again!
translations.idiomatic: The next day he petitioned again. Xianzhi told him, "I already have enough retainers on my roster—why keep coming back?

sentences.zh: 常清怒，倨謂仙芝曰：「常清慕公高義，願事鞭轡，所以無媒而前，何見拒之深乎？

translations.literal: Changqing grew angry and said haughtily to Xianzhi: "Changqing admires your lofty integrity and wishes to serve at your reins; that is why I came forward without a go-between—why do you reject me so deeply?
translations.idiomatic: Changqing grew angry and said boldly to Xianzhi, "I admire your integrity and wish to serve at your side—that is why I came unintroduced. Why reject me so harshly?

sentences.zh: 公若方圓取人，則士大夫所望；

translations.literal: If you take men by their capacity and integrity, that is what the scholar-official class hopes for;
translations.idiomatic: If you judge men by talent and character, that is what gentlemen expect;

sentences.zh: 若以貌取人，恐失之子羽矣！」

translations.literal: if you take men by appearance, I fear you will lose a Ziyu!"
translations.idiomatic: but if you judge by looks alone, you may miss another Ziyu!"

sentences.zh: 仙芝猶未納。

translations.literal: Xianzhi still did not accept him.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi still would not take him on.

sentences.zh: 常清自爾候仙芝出入，晨夕不離其門，凡數十日，仙芝不得已，補為傔。

translations.literal: From then on Changqing waited on Xianzhi's comings and goings, morning and evening never leaving his gate; after several tens of days Xianzhi had no choice and appointed him a retainer.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Changqing attended Xianzhi's comings and goings, never leaving his gate from dawn till dusk. After some ten days Xianzhi gave in and made him a retainer.

sentences.zh: 開元末，會達奚部落背叛，自黑山北向，西趣碎葉，玄宗敕靈察邀擊之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era, the Tatabi tribe rebelled, marching north from Black Mountain and turning west toward Suyab; Emperor Xuanzong ordered Lingcha to intercept and attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Near the close of the Kaiyuan reign, the Tatabi tribe rose in revolt, advancing north from Black Mountain and striking west toward Suyab. Emperor Xuanzong commanded Fumeng Lingcha to intercept and destroy them.

sentences.zh: 靈察使仙芝以二千騎自副城向北至綾嶺下，遇賊擊之。

translations.literal: Lingcha dispatched Xianzhi with two thousand cavalry from Fucheng northward to the foot of Ling Ridge, where they encountered the rebels and attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Lingcha sent Gao Xianzhi with two thousand horsemen from Fucheng north to the base of Ling Ridge, where they met the enemy and gave battle.

sentences.zh: 達奚行遠，人馬皆疲，斬殺略盡。

translations.literal: The Tatabi had marched far; men and horses were exhausted, and nearly all were cut down and killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Tatabi had come a great distance, and their men and horses were spent; the Tang forces cut them down until scarcely any remained.

sentences.zh: 常清於幕中潛作捷書，具言次舍井泉，遇賊形勢，克獲謀略，事頗精審。

translations.literal: Changqing secretly drafted the victory report in the headquarters, fully describing encampments and wells, the situation upon meeting the enemy, the strategy of capture and victory—everything in meticulous detail.
translations.idiomatic: In the command tent, Feng Changqing secretly composed the victory dispatch, recounting in precise detail every halt and watering place, the encounter with the enemy, and the tactics by which victory was won.

sentences.zh: 仙芝所欲言，無不周悉，仙芝大駭異之。

translations.literal: Everything Xianzhi would have wanted to say was fully covered; Xianzhi was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing Xianzhi himself would have wished to add was left unsaid, and he was deeply astonished.

sentences.zh: 仙芝軍回，靈察賞勞，仙芝去奴襪帶刀見。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi's army returned, Lingcha rewarded them; Xianzhi had his attendant remove his servant's foot-wrappings, gird on a sword, and brought him forward to be seen.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned and Lingcha distributed rewards, Xianzhi had his attendant Feng Changqing strip off the foot-cloths of servitude, belt on a sword, and present him before the assembly.

sentences.zh: 判官劉眺、獨孤峻等逆問之曰：「前者捷書，誰之所作？

translations.literal: The adjutants Liu Tiao and Dugu Jun and others pressed him, asking: "That victory report from before—who wrote it?
translations.idiomatic: The adjutants Liu Tiao, Dugu Jun, and others pressed forward and asked, "That victory report we received earlier—who wrote it?

sentences.zh: 副大使幕下何得有如此人」仙芝曰：「即仙芝傔人封常清也。」

translations.literal: "How could the Deputy Commissioner's staff have such a person?" Xianzhi said: "It is none other than my attendant Feng Changqing."
translations.idiomatic: "How could the deputy commissioner's staff harbor such a man?" Xianzhi replied, "None other than my own attendant, Feng Changqing."

sentences.zh: 眺等揖仙芝，命常清進坐，與語如舊相識，眾人方異之。

translations.literal: Tiao and the others bowed to Xianzhi, ordered Changqing to come forward and be seated, and conversed with him as with an old acquaintance; only then did the assembly find it remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tiao and the others bowed to Xianzhi, then summoned Changqing forward to take a seat and spoke with him as though he were an old acquaintance; only then did the company marvel at him.

sentences.zh: 以破達奚功，授疊州地下戍主，便以為判官。

translations.literal: For his achievement in defeating the Tatabi, he was appointed chief of the Diezhou underground garrison post, and concurrently made adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in crushing the Tatabi, he was appointed warden of the subterranean garrison at Die Prefecture and at once made adjutant.

sentences.zh: 累以軍功授鎮將、果毅、折沖。

translations.literal: Through repeated military achievements he was appointed fort commander, guoyi officer, and zhechong commander.
translations.idiomatic: By successive feats of arms he rose through the ranks of fort commander, guoyi officer, and zhechong commander.

sentences.zh: 天寶六年，從仙芝破小勃律。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao, he followed Xianzhi in the conquest of Lesser Bolü.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianbao, he followed Xianzhi in the campaign that brought down Lesser Bolü.

sentences.zh: 十二月，仙芝代夫蒙靈察為安西節度使，便奏常清為慶王府錄事參軍，充節度判官，賜紫金魚袋。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xianzhi replaced Fumeng Lingcha as Military Commissioner of Anxi, and immediately memorialized to appoint Changqing as Registrar in the Prince of Qing's household, serving as adjutant to the commissioner, and granted him the purple-gold fish tally pouch.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Xianzhi succeeded Fumeng Lingcha as military commissioner of Anxi and at once recommended Changqing as registrar in the household of the Prince of Qing, with concurrent appointment as adjutant to the commissioner, and bestowed upon him the purple-gold fish tally.

sentences.zh: 尋加朝散大夫，專知四鎮倉庫、屯田、甲仗、支度、營田事。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was further promoted to Master of Spreading Morality, placed exclusively in charge of the four garrisons' granaries, garrison agriculture, armor and weapons, supply accounting, and military colony affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Master of Spreading Morality and given sole charge of the granaries, garrison farms, armor and weapons, supply accounts, and military colonies of the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 仙芝每出征討，常令常清知留後事。

translations.literal: Whenever Xianzhi set out on campaign, he regularly had Changqing manage rear-affairs in his absence.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xianzhi marched out on campaign, he invariably left Changqing in charge of affairs behind the lines.

sentences.zh: 常清有才學，果決。

translations.literal: Changqing had talent and learning, and was resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing was a man of learning and ability, and decisive in action.

sentences.zh: 知留後時，仙芝乳母子鄭德詮已為郎將，德銓母在宅內，仙芝視之如兄弟，家事皆令知之，威望動三軍。

translations.literal: While managing rear affairs, Xianzhi's wet-nurse's son Zheng Dequan was already a colonel; Dequan's mother lived within the residence, and Xianzhi treated her son like a brother—all household matters were entrusted to Changqing's knowledge, and his prestige moved the entire army.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as rear-affairs commissioner, Xianzhi's foster brother Zheng Dequan already held the rank of colonel; Dequan's mother lived in the residence, and Xianzhi treated the household as his own kin, entrusting all domestic affairs to Changqing's oversight until his authority commanded the whole army.

sentences.zh: 常清出回，諸將皆引前，德詮見常清出其門，素易之，自後走馬突常清而去。

translations.literal: When Changqing came out on his return, the generals all stepped forward; Dequan saw Changqing emerge from the gate, had always looked down on him, and now rode his horse from behind, charging past Changqing and away.
translations.idiomatic: When Changqing came out on his rounds, the generals all stepped forward to greet him; Dequan, seeing him leave the gate, whom he had always held in contempt, spurred his horse from behind and galloped past Changqing without a word.

sentences.zh: 常清至使院，命左右密引至，厅連節度使宅院，凡經數重門，德詮既過，命隨後閉之。

translations.literal: Changqing reached the commissioner's office and ordered his attendants to secretly escort Dequan there; the hall connected to the commissioner's residence compound, passing through several gates in succession, and once Dequan had passed through, he ordered the gates closed behind him.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing went to the commissioner's hall and secretly ordered his men to bring Dequan there; the hall opened onto the commissioner's residential compound through several successive gates, and once Dequan had passed through, Changqing had each gate closed behind him.

sentences.zh: 德詮至，常清離席謂之曰：「常清起自細微，預中丞兵馬使傔，中丞再不納，郎將豈不知乎？

translations.literal: When Dequan arrived, Changqing rose from his seat and said to him: "Changqing rose from humble origins, becoming attendant to the Vice Commissioner and troop marshal; the Vice Commissioner twice refused to accept me—surely the Colonel knows of this?
translations.idiomatic: When Dequan arrived, Changqing rose from his seat and said, "I began in the humblest station and entered the Vice Commissioner's service as his attendant; twice he refused to take me on—surely the colonel knows this?

sentences.zh: 今中丞過聽，以常清為留後使，郎將何得無禮，對中使相淩！」

translations.literal: Now the Vice Commissioner, overestimating my merits, has appointed me rear-affairs commissioner—how can the Colonel behave without courtesy and publicly insult an imperial envoy!
translations.idiomatic: Now the Vice Commissioner, in excessive generosity, has made me rear-affairs commissioner—how can the colonel show such disrespect and publicly humiliate an imperial representative!

sentences.zh: 因叱之曰：「郎將須暫死以肅軍容。」

translations.literal: He then rebuked him, saying: "The Colonel must briefly die to restore military discipline."
translations.idiomatic: Then he shouted at him, "The colonel must die for a moment to restore discipline in the ranks."

sentences.zh: 因令勒回，杖六十，面仆地，曳出。

translations.literal: He ordered him brought back, beaten sixty strokes; Dequan fell face-down and was dragged out.
translations.idiomatic: He had Dequan seized, beaten sixty strokes with the staff, struck face-down to the ground, and dragged out.

sentences.zh: 仙芝妻及乳母於門外號哭救之，不得，因以其狀上仙芝。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's wife and wet-nurse wailed outside the gate pleading for him, to no avail; they then submitted a report of the incident to Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's wife and foster mother wailed at the gate, begging for mercy in vain, and then laid the matter before Xianzhi in a written report.

sentences.zh: 仙芝覽之，驚曰：「已死矣！」

translations.literal: Xianzhi read it and exclaimed in alarm: "He is already dead!
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi read the report and cried out in alarm, "He is already dead!

sentences.zh: 及見常清，遂無一言，常清亦不之謝。

translations.literal: When he saw Changqing, he said nothing at all; Changqing likewise did not apologize to him.
translations.idiomatic: When he met Changqing face to face, he said not a word; nor did Changqing offer any apology.

sentences.zh: 諸大將有罪者，擊殺二人，於是軍中股忄栗。

translations.literal: Of the major generals who had committed offenses, two were beaten to death; thereafter the army trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Two senior generals who had been guilty of offenses were beaten to death, and from that moment the whole army trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 十載，仙芝改西節度使，奏常清為判官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Xianzhi was transferred to Western Military Commissioner and memorialized to appoint Changqing as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianbao, Xianzhi was reassigned as military commissioner of the west and recommended Changqing once again as his adjutant.

sentences.zh: 王正見為安西節度，奏常清為四鎮支度營田副使、行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Wang Zhengjian became Military Commissioner of Anxi, he memorialized to appoint Changqing Deputy Commissioner for supply and military colonies of the Four Garrisons, and Campaign Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhengjian took command in Anxi, he recommended Changqing as deputy commissioner for supply and military colonies of the Four Garrisons and as campaign marshal.

sentences.zh: 十一載，正見死，乃以常清為安西副大都護，攝御史中丞，持節充安西四鎮節度、經略、支度、營田副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Zhengjian died, and Changqing was appointed Deputy Grand Protector of Anxi, acting Censor-in-Chief, bearing the imperial credential as Deputy Commissioner for the Military Commission, Frontier Strategy, Supply, and Military Colonies of the Anxi Four Garrisons, managing commissioner affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, after Zhengjian's death, Changqing was made deputy grand protector of Anxi, acting censor-in-chief, and with imperial commission was appointed deputy commissioner for the military administration, frontier strategy, supply, and military colonies of the Anxi Four Garrisons, with full authority over the command.

sentences.zh: 十三載入朝，攝御史大夫，仍與一子五品官，賜第一區，亡父母皆贈封爵。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he entered court; he was acting Chief Censor, and a fifth-rank post was granted to one of his sons, a premier residence was bestowed, and his deceased parents were both posthumously ennobled.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he came to court and was named acting chief censor; one of his sons received a fifth-rank appointment, he was granted a first-rank residence, and both his deceased parents were posthumously ennobled.

sentences.zh: 俄而北庭都護程千里入為右金吾大將軍，仍令常清權知北庭都護，持節充伊西節度等使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Grand Protector of Beiting Cheng Qianli entered the capital as Right General of the Gold Crow Guard; Changqing was temporarily appointed to administer Beiting Grand Protectorate, bearing the credential as Commissioner of Yixi and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Cheng Qianli, grand protector of Beiting, was recalled to the capital as right general of the Gold Crow Guard, and Changqing was temporarily entrusted with the Beiting protectorate, bearing imperial commission as commissioner of Yixi and related territories.

sentences.zh: 常清性勤儉，每出征或乘驛，私馬不過一兩匹，賞罰嚴明。

translations.literal: Changqing was by nature diligent and frugal; whenever he went on campaign or traveled by post relay, his private horses never exceeded one or two, and his rewards and punishments were strict and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing was industrious and austere by nature; on campaign or when traveling by post, he kept no more than one or two private horses, and his rewards and punishments were swift and unmistakable.

sentences.zh: 十四載，入朝，十一月，謁玄宗於華清宮。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he entered court; in the eleventh month he had an audience with Emperor Xuanzong at Huaqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he returned to court, and in the eleventh month had an audience with Emperor Xuanzong at Huaqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 時祿山已叛，玄宗言兇胡負恩之狀，何方誅討？

translations.literal: An Lushan had already rebelled; the Emperor spoke of the treacherous barbarian's ingratitude and asked by what means he could be punished and suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan had already risen in rebellion, and the Emperor spoke of the treacherous barbarian's betrayal of imperial grace, asking how he might best be punished and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 常清奏曰：「祿山領兇徒十萬，徑犯中原，太平斯久，人不知戰。

translations.literal: Changqing memorialized: "An Lushan leads a hundred thousand violent followers, marching straight to invade the Central Plains. Peace has lasted so long that the people no longer know warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing submitted a memorial: "An Lushan commands a hundred thousand hardened rebels and is marching straight upon the heartland. Peace has endured so long that the people have forgotten how to fight.

sentences.zh: 然事有逆順，勢有奇變，臣請走馬赴東京，開府庫，募驍勇，挑馬箠渡河，計日取逆胡之首懸於闕下。」

translations.literal: Yet affairs have their right and wrong, and strategic situations admit sudden turns. Your servant requests to ride at full speed to the Eastern Capital, open the treasury stores, recruit fierce warriors, lash my horse across the river, and within a counted number of days bring the rebel chieftain's head to hang beneath the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Yet right and wrong still govern affairs, and fortune can turn in an instant. Your servant begs leave to ride at full speed to the Eastern Capital, throw open the arsenals, raise the bravest fighters, whip his horse across the river, and within days bring the rebel chieftain's head to hang beneath the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 玄宗方憂，壯其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then deeply worried and took heart from his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, then heavy with anxiety, was heartened by his bold words.

sentences.zh: 翌日，以常清為范陽節度，俾募兵東討。

translations.literal: The next day he appointed Changqing Military Commissioner of Fanyang and ordered him to recruit troops and march east to suppress the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he appointed Changqing military commissioner of Fanyang and ordered him to raise troops and march east against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 其日，常清乘驛赴東京召募，旬日得兵六萬，皆傭保市井之流。

translations.literal: That same day Changqing traveled by post relay to the Eastern Capital to recruit; within ten days he gathered sixty thousand troops, all hired hands and market riffraff.
translations.idiomatic: That very day Changqing rode post to the Eastern Capital to raise an army; within ten days he had assembled sixty thousand men, all mercenaries and street rabble from the markets.

sentences.zh: 乃斫斷河陽橋，於東京為固守之備。

translations.literal: He then cut down the Heyang Bridge and made preparations to hold fast in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then destroyed the Heyang Bridge and prepared the Eastern Capital for a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 十二月，祿山渡河，陷陳留，入罌子谷，兇威轉熾，先鋒至葵園。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month An Lushan crossed the river, captured Chenliu, entered Yingzi Valley; his savage momentum grew ever fiercer, and his vanguard reached Kui Garden.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month An Lushan crossed the Yellow River, took Chenliu, and entered Yingzi Valley; his savage momentum swelled by the day, and his vanguard reached Kui Garden.

sentences.zh: 常清使驍騎與柘羯逆戰，殺賊數十百人。

translations.literal: Changqing sent crack cavalry to meet the Tuqishi in battle and killed several tens or hundreds of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing sent his best horsemen to meet the Tuqishi vanguard in battle and killed several hundred of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊大軍繼至，常清退入上東門，又戰不利，賊鼓噪於四城門入，殺掠人吏。

translations.literal: The rebel main force followed; Changqing withdrew into the Upper East Gate, fought again without success; the rebels raised a clamor at all four city gates and entered, killing and plundering officials and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel main force pressed on; Changqing fell back to the Upper East Gate and fought again without success. The rebels raised a thunderous clamor at all four gates, poured into the city, and slaughtered and plundered officials and clerks.

sentences.zh: 常清又戰於都亭驛，不勝。

translations.literal: Changqing fought again at Duting Post Station and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing gave battle again at Duting Post Station and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 退守宣仁門，又敗。

translations.literal: He retreated to hold the Xuanren Gate and was defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to hold the Xuanren Gate and was defeated once more.

sentences.zh: 乃從提象門入，倒樹以礙之。

translations.literal: He then entered through the Tixiang Gate and felled trees to obstruct pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: He then retreated through the Tixiang Gate and felled trees behind him to block pursuit.

sentences.zh: 至谷水，西奔至陜郡，遇高仙芝，具以賊勢告之。

translations.literal: Reaching Gu River, he fled west to Shaan Commandery, met Gao Xianzhi, and fully reported the enemy's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the Gu River, he fled west to Shaan Commandery, where he met Gao Xianzhi and gave him a full account of the enemy's strength.

sentences.zh: 恐賊難與爭鋒，仙芝遂退守潼關。

translations.literal: Fearing the rebels were too strong to engage head-on, Xianzhi then withdrew to hold Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the rebels too fierce to meet in open battle, Xianzhi withdrew to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 玄宗聞常清敗，削其官爵，令白衣於仙芝軍效力。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong heard of Changqing's defeat, he stripped him of rank and title and ordered him to serve in Xianzhi's army as a commoner in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor learned of Changqing's defeat, he stripped him of rank and title and ordered him to serve in Xianzhi's army as a common soldier in undyed robes.

sentences.zh: 仙芝令常清監巡左右廂諸軍，常清衣皁衣以從事。

translations.literal: Xianzhi had Changqing supervise and inspect the armies of the Left and Right wings; Changqing wore black robes in performing his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi put Changqing in charge of inspecting the Left and Right wing armies, and Changqing wore plain black garments as he went about his duties.

sentences.zh: 監軍邊令誠每事幹之。

translations.literal: The army inspector Bian Lingcheng interfered in every matter.
translations.idiomatic: The army inspector Bian Lingcheng meddled in every decision.

sentences.zh: 仙芝多不從。

translations.literal: Xianzhi often refused to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi often refused to heed him.

sentences.zh: 令誠入奏事，具言仙芝、常清逗撓奔敗之狀。

translations.literal: Lingcheng entered court to report and fully described how Xianzhi and Changqing had delayed, shirked, and fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Lingcheng returned to court and reported in full that Xianzhi and Changqing had dallied, shirked their duty, and fled in defeat.

sentences.zh: 玄宗怒，遣令誠賫敕至軍並誅之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged and dispatched Lingcheng bearing an edict to the army to execute them both.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage and sent Lingcheng back to the army with an edict ordering the execution of them both.

sentences.zh: 令誠至潼關，引常清於驛南西街，宣敕示之。

translations.literal: Lingcheng reached Tong Pass, brought Changqing to South West Street of the post station, and displayed the edict before him.
translations.idiomatic: Lingcheng arrived at Tong Pass, led Changqing to South West Street beside the post station, and read out the edict before him.

sentences.zh: 常清曰：「常清所以不死者，不忍汙國家旌麾，受戮賊手，討逆無效，死乃甘心。」

translations.literal: Changqing said: "The reason Changqing has not died until now is that I could not bear to defile the state's banners by falling to the rebels' blades; though suppressing the rebellion has failed, I can die content.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing said, "The reason I have clung to life until now is that I could not bear to see the imperial banners dishonored by dying at the rebels' hands. Though I failed to suppress the rebellion, I can die with a clear conscience.

sentences.zh: 初，常清兵敗入關，欲馳赴闕庭，至渭南，有敕令卻赴潼關，自草表待罪。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Changqing's army was defeated and he entered the pass, he had wished to ride post-haste to the imperial court; reaching Weinan, an edict ordered him to turn back to Tong Pass, and he himself drafted a memorial accepting guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after his defeat and withdrawal through the pass, he had intended to ride at once to the imperial court; but at Weinan an edict turned him back to Tong Pass, and there he drafted a memorial accepting blame.

sentences.zh: 是日臨刑，托令誠上之。

translations.literal: On the day of execution he entrusted Lingcheng to submit it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his execution he entrusted the memorial to Lingcheng for presentation to the throne.

sentences.zh: 其表曰：

translations.literal: The memorial read:
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ran as follows:

sentences.zh: 中使駱奉仙至，奉宣口敕，恕臣萬死之罪，收臣一朝之效，令臣卻赴陜州，隨高仙芝行營，。

translations.literal: "The palace envoy Luo Fengxian arrived, proclaiming an oral edict pardoning your servant's myriad capital offenses, accepting your servant's single day's service, and ordering your servant to return to Shaanzhou to follow Gao Xianzhi's field headquarters."
translations.idiomatic: "The palace envoy Luo Fengxian arrived bearing an oral edict, pardoning my countless capital crimes, accepting whatever service I might yet render, and ordering me to return to Shaanzhou and join Gao Xianzhi's field headquarters."

sentences.zh: 負斧縲囚，忽焉解縛，敗軍之將，更許增修。

translations.literal: "Bearing the axe, bound as a prisoner—I was suddenly freed from my shackles; a defeated general was yet permitted to make amends."
translations.idiomatic: "I came bound like a condemned man bearing the executioner's axe, and was suddenly released from my fetters; a defeated general was granted the chance to redeem himself."

sentences.zh: 臣常清誠歡誠喜，頓首頓首。

translations.literal: "Your servant Changqing is truly joyful, truly delighted—kowtowing, kowtowing."
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant Changqing is overcome with gratitude and joy—kowtowing, kowtowing."

sentences.zh: 臣自城陷已來，前後三度遣使奉表，具述赤心，竟不蒙引對。

translations.literal: "Since the city's fall, your servant has three times sent envoys submitting memorials, fully laying bare my loyal heart, yet was never granted an audience."
translations.idiomatic: "Since the fall of the city I have three times dispatched envoys with memorials laying bare my loyal heart, yet was never granted an audience with Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 臣之此來，非求茍活，實欲陳社稷之計，破虎狼之謀。

translations.literal: "Your servant came this time not to beg for bare life, but truly to set forth plans for the altars of state and to thwart the designs of tiger and wolf."
translations.idiomatic: "I came not to beg for my life, but to offer plans for the preservation of the realm and to break the schemes of this tiger and wolf."

sentences.zh: 冀拜首闕庭，吐心陛下，論逆胡之兵勢，陳討捍之別謀。

translations.literal: "I hoped to bow my head before the palace gates, pour out my heart before Your Majesty, discuss the rebel barbarian's military strength, and present alternative strategies for suppression and defense."
translations.idiomatic: "I had hoped to prostrate myself before the palace gates, pour out my heart to Your Majesty, assess the rebel's military strength, and propose other strategies for defense and suppression."

sentences.zh: 酬萬死之恩，以報一生之寵。

translations.literal: "To repay the grace of sparing my myriad deaths, and to requite the favor of a lifetime's patronage."
translations.idiomatic: "Thus to repay the grace of sparing my life and to answer the favor of a lifetime's trust."

sentences.zh: 豈料長安日遠，謁見無由；

translations.literal: "Who could have foreseen that Chang'an grows daily more distant, with no means to gain an audience;"
translations.idiomatic: "Who could have known that Chang'an would grow more distant with each passing day, and that I would find no path to audience;"

sentences.zh: 函谷關遙，陳情不暇！

translations.literal: "Hangu Pass lies far away—there is no time to present my plea!"
translations.idiomatic: "Hangu Pass stands between us, and I have no time left to plead my case!"

sentences.zh: 臣讀《春秋》，見狼瞫稱未獲死所，臣今獲矣。

translations.literal: "Your servant has read the Spring and Autumn Annals and seen that Lang Zhi said he had not yet found the place to die—your servant has found it now."
translations.idiomatic: "I have read the Spring and Autumn Annals and seen how Lang Zhi lamented that he had not yet found the place to die—I have found mine at last."

sentences.zh: 昨者與羯胡接戰，自今月七日交兵，至於十三日不已。

translations.literal: "Recently in battle with the Jie barbarians, fighting began on the seventh of this month and continued unceasingly until the thirteenth."
translations.idiomatic: "In recent fighting with the Jie rebels, battle was joined on the seventh of this month and did not cease until the thirteenth."

sentences.zh: 臣所將之兵，皆是烏合之徒，素未訓習。

translations.literal: "The troops your servant commanded were all a motley crowd, never trained in discipline."
translations.idiomatic: "The troops under my command were a rabble gathered overnight, never drilled in the arts of war."

sentences.zh: 率周南市人之眾，當漁陽突騎之師，尚猶殺敵塞路，血流滿野。

translations.literal: "Leading the masses of Zhou and Nan markets against the Fanyang shock cavalry, we still blocked the road with slain enemies until blood covered the fields."
translations.idiomatic: "Leading market folk from the Zhou and Nan wards against the shock cavalry of Fanyang, we still piled the slain so thick upon the road that blood soaked the fields."

sentences.zh: 臣欲挺身刃下，死節軍前，恐長逆胡之威，以挫王師之勢。

translations.literal: "Your servant wished to throw himself beneath the blades and die honorably before the ranks, but feared this would only magnify the rebel chieftain's prestige and break the imperial army's momentum."
translations.idiomatic: "I wished to throw myself beneath the enemy blades and die honorably before the ranks, but feared that doing so would only swell the rebel chieftain's arrogance and break the imperial army's spirit."

sentences.zh: 是以馳禦就日，將命歸天。

translations.literal: "Therefore I rode post-haste toward the capital, prepared to surrender my life to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: "Therefore I rode at full speed toward the capital, prepared to surrender my life to Heaven's judgment."

sentences.zh: 一期陛下斬臣於都市之下，以誡諸將；

translations.literal: "First, that Your Majesty would execute your servant beneath the marketplace as a warning to all generals;"
translations.idiomatic: "First, that Your Majesty might execute me in the public square as a warning to every general;"

sentences.zh: 二期陛下問臣以逆賊之勢，將誡諸軍；

translations.literal: "Second, that Your Majesty would question your servant about the rebel forces' strength to instruct the armies;"
translations.idiomatic: "Second, that Your Majesty might question me about the rebel's strength and so instruct the armies;"

sentences.zh: 三期陛下知臣非惜死之徒，許臣竭露。

translations.literal: "Third, that Your Majesty would know your servant is no one who clings to life, and would permit me to lay bare my utmost loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: "Third, that Your Majesty might know I am no coward who clings to life, and allow me to pour out my utmost loyalty."

sentences.zh: 臣今將死抗表，陛下或以臣失律之後，誑妄為辭；

translations.literal: "Your servant now faces death while submitting this defiant memorial; Your Majesty may take my words after military failure as deceitful pretense;"
translations.idiomatic: "I now face death while submitting this final memorial; Your Majesty may dismiss my words, after my military failure, as the deceitful excuses of a defeated man;"

sentences.zh: 陛下或以臣欲盡所忠，肝膽見察。

translations.literal: "Or Your Majesty may see that your servant wishes to exhaust all loyalty, with heart and liver laid bare for inspection."
translations.idiomatic: "Or Your Majesty may recognize that I seek only to exhaust every ounce of loyalty I possess, with heart and liver laid bare before you."

sentences.zh: 臣死之後，望陛下不輕此賊，無忘臣言，則冀社稷復安，逆胡敗覆，臣之所願畢矣。

translations.literal: "After your servant's death, I hope Your Majesty will not underestimate this rebel and will not forget my words—then the altars of state may be restored to peace, the rebel chieftain overturned and destroyed, and your servant's wishes fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: "After my death, I pray that Your Majesty will not underestimate this rebel or forget my words—then the altars of state may be restored, the rebel chieftain overthrown, and my last wish fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 仰天飲鴆，向日封章，即為屍諫之臣，死作聖朝之鬼。

translations.literal: "Looking up to Heaven, drinking poison, facing the sun with sealed memorial—I become at once a minister who remonstrates with my corpse, and in death a ghost of the sacred dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: "Raising my eyes to Heaven, drinking poison, facing the sun with this sealed memorial—I become a minister who remonstrates with his corpse, and in death a loyal ghost of the sacred dynasty."

sentences.zh: 若使歿而有知，必結草軍前。

translations.literal: "If the dead retain awareness, I shall surely tie grass before the army ranks."
translations.idiomatic: "If the dead retain consciousness, I shall surely repay my debt with knotted grass before the army's ranks."

sentences.zh: 回風陣上，引王師之旗鼓，平寇賊之戈鋋。

translations.literal: "Turn the wind upon the battle line, guide the imperial army's banners and drums, and level the bandits' spears and blades."
translations.idiomatic: "May I turn the wind upon the battle line, guide the banners and drums of the imperial host, and sweep away the rebels' spears and blades."

sentences.zh: 生死酬恩，不任感激，臣常清無任永辭聖代悲戀之至。

translations.literal: "In life and death repaying grace—I cannot bear the fullness of gratitude; your servant Changqing cannot bear the utmost sorrow of forever parting from this sacred age."
translations.idiomatic: "Life and death alike I devote to repaying grace; words cannot contain my gratitude. Your servant Changqing bows in eternal farewell, overwhelmed with sorrow at parting from this sacred age."

sentences.zh: 常清既刑，陳其屍於蘧蒢上。

translations.literal: Once Changqing was executed, his corpse was displayed on a coarse mat.
translations.idiomatic: After the execution, Changqing's body was laid out on a straw mat.

sentences.zh: 仙芝歸至厅，令誠索陌刀手百餘人隨而從之，曰：「大夫亦有恩命。」

translations.literal: Xianzhi returned to the hall; Lingcheng summoned more than a hundred saber troops to follow him, saying: "The Grand Marshal also has an edict of grace.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi returned to the hall, and Lingcheng gathered more than a hundred saber troops to follow him, saying, "The Grand Marshal has an edict as well.

sentences.zh: 仙芝遽下，遂至常清所刑處。

translations.literal: Xianzhi quickly dismounted and went straight to the place where Changqing had been executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi dismounted at once and went directly to the place where Changqing had been executed.

sentences.zh: 仙芝曰：「我退，罪也，死不辭；

translations.literal: Xianzhi said: "My retreat was a crime—I do not refuse death;
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi said, "My retreat was a crime, and I do not shrink from death;

sentences.zh: 然以我為減截兵糧及賜物等，則誣我也。」

translations.literal: But to charge me with cutting rations and plundering issued goods—that is slander against me.
translations.idiomatic: but to accuse me of withholding rations and plundering issued goods—that is a lie.

sentences.zh: 謂令誠曰：「上是天，下是地，兵士皆在，足下豈不知乎！」

translations.literal: He said to Lingcheng: "Above is Heaven, below is Earth, and the soldiers are all here—surely you know this!"
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Lingcheng and said, "Heaven is above, earth is below, and the soldiers stand witness—surely you know the truth!"

sentences.zh: 其召募兵排列在外，素愛仙芝，仙芝呼謂之曰：「我於京中召兒郎輩，雖得少許物，裝束亦未能足，方與君輩破賊，然後取高官重賞。

translations.literal: His recruited troops stood arrayed outside; they had always loved Xianzhi. Xianzhi called out to them: "When I recruited you lads in the capital, though you received a few supplies, your equipment was still inadequate—we were just about to break the rebels together and then claim high rank and heavy rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The troops he had recruited stood drawn up outside; they had always held Xianzhi in affection. He called out to them, "When I recruited you men in the capital, you received only scant supplies and your equipment was never complete—we were on the verge of breaking the rebels together and then claiming high rank and rich reward.

sentences.zh: 不謂賊勢憑陵，引軍至此，亦欲固守潼關故也。

translations.literal: I never expected the rebels' momentum would press upon us and drive the army here—we also intended to hold Tong Pass firm.
translations.idiomatic: I never dreamed the rebel tide would overwhelm us and drive the army to this pass—we came here precisely to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 我若實有此，君輩即言實；

translations.literal: If I truly did such things, you say so truthfully;
translations.idiomatic: If I truly did these things, say so plainly;

sentences.zh: 我若實無之，君輩當言枉。」

translations.literal: If I truly did not, you must say it was false."
translations.idiomatic: If I did not, say that I have been wronged."

sentences.zh: 兵齊呼曰：「枉」，其聲殷地。

translations.literal: The soldiers all shouted: "False!"—their voices thundered against the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers shouted as one: "Wronged!"—their voices shook the ground.

sentences.zh: 仙芝又目常清之屍，謂之曰：「封二，子從微至著，我則引拔子為我判官，俄又代我為節度使，今日又與子同死於此，豈命也夫！」

translations.literal: Xianzhi then looked at Changqing's corpse and said to it: "Second Brother Feng, you rose from obscurity to eminence—I promoted you to be my adjutant, and soon you replaced me as military commissioner; today we die together here—is this not fate!
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi then gazed at Changqing's corpse and said, "Second Brother Feng, you rose from nothing to greatness—I lifted you up as my adjutant, and soon you succeeded me as commissioner; today we die together in this place—is this not fate?

sentences.zh: 遂斬之。

translations.literal: And then he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Then they beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰，突騎施首領哥舒部落之裔也。

translations.literal: Geshu Han was a descendant of the Geshu tribe, chieftains of the Tuqishi.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han was descended from the Geshu tribe, chieftains of the Tuqishi confederation.

sentences.zh: 蕃人多以部落稱姓，因以為氏。

translations.literal: Many barbarian people took their tribe names as surnames, and thus it became his family name.
translations.idiomatic: Among the frontier peoples it was common to take one's tribal name as a surname, and so the name became his family line.

sentences.zh: 祖沮，左清道率。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Ju, Left Clear-the-Way Commander.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Ju, commander of the Left Clear-the-Way unit.

sentences.zh: 父道元，安西副都護，世居安西。

translations.literal: His father Daoyuan was Deputy Protector-General of Anxi; the family had long resided in Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daoyuan served as deputy protector-general of Anxi, and the family had lived there for generations.

sentences.zh: 翰家富於財，倜儻任俠，好然諾，縱蒲酒。

translations.literal: The Han family was wealthy in property. He was free-spirited and chivalrous, fond of keeping his word, and given to gambling and wine.
translations.idiomatic: The Han family was rich. Ge Shuhan was bold and chivalrous, delighted in honoring his promises, and prone to gambling and drinking.

sentences.zh: 年四十，遭父喪，三年客居京師，為長安尉不禮，慨然發憤折節，仗劍之河西。

translations.literal: At the age of forty he suffered his father's death. For three years he lodged in the capital as a guest. The warden of Chang'an treated him discourteously. Indignant, he resolved to reform himself, took up sword, and went to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: When he was forty, his father died. He spent three years living in the capital as a guest, where the warden of Chang'an slighted him. Stung to anger, he resolved to change his ways, took up the sword, and made for Hexi.

sentences.zh: 初事節度使王倕，倕攻新城，使翰經略，三軍無不震懾。

translations.literal: At first he served Military Commissioner Wang Yun. When Yun attacked Xincheng, he had Han oversee operations; the whole army was without exception awed and intimidated.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under the military commissioner Wang Yun. When Yun attacked Xincheng, he put Han in charge of the campaign, and the entire army was awestruck.

sentences.zh: 後節度使王忠嗣補為衙將。

translations.literal: Later Military Commissioner Wang Zhongsi appointed him a headquarters guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: Later the military commissioner Wang Zhongsi appointed him a guard officer on his staff.

sentences.zh: 翰好讀《左氏春秋傳》及《漢書》，疏財重氣，士多歸之。

translations.literal: Han loved reading the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Book of Han. He was generous with money and valued loyalty; many men rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: Han loved to read the Zuo Commentary and the Book of Han. He was free with his wealth and held loyalty dear, and many men gathered around him.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣以為大鬥軍副使，嘗使翰討吐蕃於新城，有同列為副者，見翰禮倨，不為用，翰怒，撾殺之，軍中股怵。

translations.literal: Zhongsi made him deputy commissioner of the Great Battle Army. Once he sent Han to campaign against the Tibetans at Xincheng. There was a fellow deputy who, seeing Han's arrogant manner, would not obey him. Han grew furious and beat him to death, striking terror through the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi appointed him deputy commissioner of the Great Battle Army. On one occasion he sent Han to attack the Tibetans at Xincheng. A fellow deputy, offended by Han's haughty bearing, refused to follow his orders. Han flew into a rage and beat the man to death, throwing the army into dread.

sentences.zh: 遷左衛郎將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Guard Corps commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commandant of the Left Guard Corps.

sentences.zh: 後吐蕃寇邊，翰拒之於苦拔海，其眾三行，從山差池而下，翰持半段槍當其鋒擊之，三行皆敗，無不摧靡，由是知名。

translations.literal: Later, when the Tibetans raided the frontier, Han repelled them at Kubohai. Their force came in three columns descending unevenly from the mountains. Han took a half-length spear and struck their vanguard; all three columns were defeated and utterly crushed, and he became renowned thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Tibetans raided the border, Han drove them back at Kubohai. Their army advanced in three ranks, winding down from the mountains in staggered lines. Han met their vanguard with a shortened spear and shattered all three ranks until nothing stood before him, and from that day his name was known.

sentences.zh: 天寶六載，擢授右武衛員外將軍，充隴西節度副使、都知關西兵馬使、河源軍使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao he was elevated to acting general of the Right Martial Guard, concurrently serving as deputy military commissioner of Longxi, overseer of Guanxi troops and horses, and commander of the Heyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianbao he was promoted to acting general of the Right Martial Guard and appointed deputy military commissioner of Longxi, overseer of all troops and horses west of the passes, and commander of the Heyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 先是，吐蕃每至麥熟時，即率部眾至積石軍獲取之，共呼為「吐蕃麥莊」，前後無敢拒之者。

translations.literal: Previously, whenever the wheat ripened, the Tibetans would lead their bands to Jishi Army post to seize the harvest. This was commonly called the Tibetan wheat farms, and for years none dared resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, whenever the wheat ripened the Tibetans would lead their followers to the Jishi garrison to carry off the crop. People called it the Tibetan wheat estate, and for years no one had dared stand in their way.

sentences.zh: 至是，翰使王難得、楊景暉等潛引兵至積石軍，設伏以待之。

translations.literal: At this time Han secretly sent Wang Nande, Yang Jinghui, and others to lead troops to Jishi Army post and lay an ambush to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Han now secretly sent Wang Nande, Yang Jinghui, and others to bring troops to Jishi garrison and set an ambush.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃以五千騎至，翰於城中率驍勇馳擊，殺之略盡，餘或挺走，伏兵邀擊，匹馬不還。

translations.literal: The Tibetans arrived with five thousand horsemen. Han led his best fighters from the city in a charge and killed nearly all of them. Those who fled were intercepted by the ambush; not a single horse returned.
translations.idiomatic: When five thousand Tibetan horsemen arrived, Han led the city's fiercest warriors in a galloping attack and killed nearly all of them. The survivors who bolted were cut off by the ambush, and not one horse made it back.

sentences.zh: 翰有家奴曰左軍，年十五六，亦有膂力。

translations.literal: Han had a household slave named Zuojun, fifteen or sixteen years old, who also possessed great strength.
translations.idiomatic: Han kept a household slave named Zuojun, fifteen or sixteen years old, who was likewise strong.

sentences.zh: 翰善使槍，追賊及之，以槍搭其肩而喝之，賊驚顧，翰從而刺其喉，皆剔高三五尺而墮，無不死者。

translations.literal: Han was skilled with the spear. Pursuing the enemy till he caught up, he would touch the spear to the man's shoulder and shout; when the man turned in alarm, Han would thrust into his throat, impaling him three to five feet high before he fell—none survived.
translations.idiomatic: Han was master of the spear. When he overtook a fleeing enemy he would lay the spear across the man's shoulder and shout; startled, the man would turn, and Han would drive the point into his throat, lifting him three or five feet into the air before he fell. None lived.

sentences.zh: 左車輒下馬斬首，率以為常。

translations.literal: Zuoche would always dismount and cut off the head, and this became their custom.
translations.idiomatic: Zuoche would always dismount and take the head—a routine they followed every time.

sentences.zh: 其冬，玄宗在華清宮，王忠嗣被劾。

translations.literal: That winter, Emperor Xuanzong was at Huaqing Palace when Wang Zhongsi was impeached.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, while Emperor Xuanzong was at Huaqing Palace, Wang Zhongsi was impeached.

sentences.zh: 敕召翰至，與語悅之，遂以為鴻臚卿，兼西平郡太守，攝御史中丞，代忠嗣為隴右節度支度營田副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Han to court. The emperor was pleased in conversation with him and appointed him Minister of Ceremonies, concurrently governor of Xiping commandery and acting censor-in-chief, replacing Zhongsi as deputy commissioner of the Longyou circuit for supplies, frontier colonies, and military affairs, with charge of circuit administration.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order summoned Han to court.
