The emperor found him pleasing in conversation and appointed him Minister of Ceremonies, concurrently governor of Xiping commandery and acting censor-in-chief, with Han replacing Zhongsi as deputy commissioner of the Longyou circuit for supplies, frontier colonies, and military affairs, with full charge of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 仍極言救忠嗣，上起入禁中，翰叩頭隨之而前，言詞慷慨，聲淚俱下，帝感而寬之，貶忠嗣為漢陽太守，朝廷義而壯之。

translations.literal: He further pleaded strenuously to save Zhongsi. The emperor rose and entered the inner palace; Han kowtowed and followed forward, speaking with passionate eloquence, voice and tears together. The emperor was moved and showed leniency, demoting Zhongsi to governor of Hanyang. The court admired Han's righteous courage.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke at length to save Zhongsi. When the emperor rose and withdrew into the palace, Han kowtowed and pressed forward after him, speaking with fierce conviction until voice and tears mingled. Moved, the emperor relented and demoted Zhongsi to governor of Hanyang. The court honored Han for his righteous boldness.

sentences.zh: 明年，築神威軍於青海上，吐蕃至，攻破之；

translations.literal: The next year he built Shenwei Army on the Qinghai. When the Tibetans came, they captured and destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he built Shenwei garrison on the Qinghai. When Tibetans arrived, they broke in and destroyed it.

sentences.zh: 又築城於青海中龍駒島，有白龍見，遂名為應龍城，吐蕃屏跡不敢近青海。

translations.literal: He also built a fort on Longju Island in the midst of Qinghai. A white dragon appeared, so it was named Yinglong Fort. The Tibetans withdrew and dared not approach Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: He also built a city on Longju Island in the middle of Qinghai. A white dragon was seen, and the place was therefore named Yinglong City. The Tibetans withdrew and no longer dared approach Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃保石堡城，路遠而險，久不拔。

translations.literal: The Tibetans held Shibao Fort; the route was long and perilous, and for a long time it could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans held Shibao Fort. The road was long and dangerous, and for a long time it could not be captured.

sentences.zh: 八載，以朔方、河東群牧十萬眾委翰總統攻石堡城。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, one hundred thousand men from the Shufang and Hedong horse-pasture offices were entrusted to Han to command the assault on Shibao Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, one hundred thousand men from the Shufang and Hedong horse-pasture offices were placed under Han's overall command to attack Shibao Fort.

sentences.zh: 翰使麾下將高秀巖、張守瑜進攻，不旬日而拔之。

translations.literal: Han sent his generals Gao Xiuyan and Zhang Shouyu to attack; within ten days they captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent his subordinate generals Gao Xiuyan and Zhang Shouyu to press the attack, and within ten days the fort fell.

sentences.zh: 上錄其功，拜特進、鴻臚員外卿，與一子五品官，賜物千匹、莊宅各一所，加攝御史大夫。

translations.literal: The emperor recorded his merit, appointing him Special Promotion and acting Minister of Ceremonies, granting one son a fifth-rank office, bestowing a thousand lengths of goods and one manor and estate each, and adding the acting post of chief censor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recorded his achievements and appointed him to Special Promotion and acting Minister of Ceremonies, granted one of his sons a fifth-rank office, bestowed a thousand lengths of goods plus a manor and a residence, and added the acting post of chief censor.

sentences.zh: 十一載，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was further given the Palace-and-Procession status of Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was further granted the honorary rank of Palace-and-Procession status equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 翰素與祿山、思順不協，上每和解之為兄弟。

translations.literal: Han had long been at odds with An Lushan and An Sishun; the emperor often reconciled them as sworn brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Han had long been on bad terms with An Lushan and An Sishun, and the emperor often patched up their quarrels by treating them as sworn brothers.

sentences.zh: 其冬，祿山、思順、翰並來朝，上使內侍高力士及中貴人於京城東駙馬崔惠童池亭宴會。

translations.literal: That winter Lushan, Sishun, and Han all came to court. The emperor had the eunuch Gao Lishi and palace dignitaries host a banquet at the pavilion by the pool of Cui Huitong, imperial son-in-law, east of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Lushan, Sishun, and Han all came to court together. The emperor had the eunuch Gao Lishi and other palace dignitaries host a banquet at the pool pavilion of Cui Huitong, an imperial son-in-law, east of the capital.

sentences.zh: 翰母尉遲氏，於闐之族也。

translations.literal: Han's mother was Lady Yuchi, of Khotanese descent.
translations.idiomatic: Han's mother was Lady Yuchi, of Khotanese stock.

sentences.zh: 祿山以思順惡翰，嘗銜之，至是忽謂翰曰：「我父是胡，母是突厥；

translations.literal: Because Sishun disliked Han, Lushan had long harbored resentment toward him. At this point he suddenly said to Han: My father was a Hu and my mother was a Turk.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan bore a grudge against Han because Sishun disliked him. Suddenly he said to Han, "My father was a Hu and my mother was a Turk.

sentences.zh: 公父是突厥，母是胡。

translations.literal: Your father was a Turk and your mother was a Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Your father was a Turk and your mother was a Hu.

sentences.zh: 與公族類同，何不相親乎？」

translations.literal: Our peoples are alike—why should we not be close?
translations.idiomatic: We are of the same kind—why should we not be kin?

sentences.zh: 翰應之曰：「古人雲，野狐向窟嗥，不祥，以其忘本也。

translations.literal: Han replied: The ancients said that when a wild fox howls toward its den, it is an ill omen, because it has forgotten its roots.
translations.idiomatic: Han answered, "The ancients said that when a wild fox howls toward its lair it is an ill omen, for it has forgotten where it came from.

sentences.zh: 敢不盡心焉！」

translations.literal: How could I fail to give you my whole heart!
translations.idiomatic: How could I fail to give you my whole heart!

sentences.zh: 祿山以為譏其胡也，大怒，罵翰曰：「突厥敢如此耶！」

translations.literal: Lushan took this as a mockery of his Hu ancestry and flew into a rage, cursing Han: How dare a Turk behave like this!
translations.idiomatic: Lushan took this as a slur on his Hu blood and raged, cursing Han: "How dare a Turk speak to me like this!"

sentences.zh: 翰欲應之，高力士目翰，翰遂止。

translations.literal: Han was about to answer back, but Gao Lishi signaled him with his eyes, and Han stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Han was about to retort, but Gao Lishi caught his eye, and Han held his tongue.

sentences.zh: 十二載，進封涼國公，食實封三百戶，加河西節度使，尋封西平郡王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang with three hundred revenue households, made military commissioner of Hexi, and soon thereafter created Prince of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was advanced to Duke of Liang with three hundred revenue households, appointed military commissioner of Hexi, and soon after enfeoffed as Prince of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 時楊國忠有隙於祿山，頻奏其反狀，故厚賞翰以親結之。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Guozhong was estranged from Lushan and repeatedly reported signs of rebellion, so he richly rewarded Han to bind him in friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong was then at odds with Lushan and repeatedly memorialized the throne with evidence of his disloyalty, so he lavished rewards on Han to win him over.

sentences.zh: 十三載，拜太子太保，更加實封三百戶，又兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, granted another three hundred revenue households, and again made chief censor concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, given another three hundred revenue households, and again made chief censor in concurrent office.

sentences.zh: 翰好飲酒，頗恣聲色。

translations.literal: Han loved wine and indulged freely in music and women.
translations.idiomatic: Han loved drinking and indulged freely in music and women.

sentences.zh: 至土門軍，入浴室，遘風疾，絕倒良久乃蘇。

translations.literal: When he reached Tumen Army post, he entered the bathhouse, was stricken with wind illness, collapsed unconscious for a long time before reviving.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Tumen garrison and entered the bathhouse, he was struck by wind illness, collapsed unconscious, and lay insensible for a long time before he came to.

sentences.zh: 因入京，廢疾於家。

translations.literal: He therefore entered the capital and lived at home incapacitated by illness.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to the capital and remained at home, crippled by his illness.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山反，上以封常清、高仙芝喪敗，召翰入，拜為皇太子先鋒兵馬元帥，以田良丘為御史中丞，充行軍司馬，以王思禮、鉗耳大福、李承光、蘇法鼎、管崇嗣及蕃將火拔歸仁、李武定、渾萼、契苾寧等為裨將，河隴、朔方兵及蕃兵與高仙芝舊卒共二十萬，拒賊於潼關。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, because Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi had been defeated and killed, the emperor summoned Han, appointed him Grand Marshal of the Heir Apparent's Vanguard Army, made Tian Liangqiu acting censor-in-chief and expedition chief of staff, and Wang Sili, Qian'er Dafu, Li Chengguang, Su Fading, Guan Chongsi, and the foreign generals Huoba Guiren, Li Wuding, Hun E, and Qibi Ning staff generals, with Hexi, Longyou, Shufang troops and foreign soldiers together with Gao Xianzhi's old troops totaling two hundred thousand, to resist the rebels at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, the emperor—after Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi had been defeated and executed—recalled Han and appointed him grand marshal of the heir apparent's vanguard army. Tian Liangqiu served as acting censor-in-chief and expedition chief of staff; Wang Sili, Qian'er Dafu, Li Chengguang, Su Fading, Guan Chongsi, and the foreign generals Huoba Guiren, Li Wuding, Hun E, and Qibi Ning served as staff generals. With troops from Hexi, Longyou, and Shufang, foreign auxiliaries, and Gao Xianzhi's old soldiers—two hundred thousand in all—he was to hold the rebels at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 上御勤政樓勞遣之，百僚出餞於郊。

translations.literal: The emperor attended the Qinzheng Tower to honor and send him off; the hundred officials went out to the suburbs to bid farewell.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the Qinzheng Tower to honor and send him forth, and the whole court went out to the suburbs to see him off.

sentences.zh: 十五載，加翰尚書左僕射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was further made Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat and co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was further appointed Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat and given the rank of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 翰至潼關，或勸翰曰：「祿山阻兵，以誅楊國忠為名，公若留兵三萬守關，悉以精銳回誅國忠，此漢挫七國之計也，公以為何如？」

translations.literal: When Han reached Tong Pass, someone advised him: Lushan has raised troops under the pretext of executing Yang Guozhong. If you leave thirty thousand men to hold the pass and bring all your best troops back to kill Guozhong, this is the Han stratagem that broke the Seven Kingdoms—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: When Han arrived at Tong Pass, someone urged him: "Lushan has taken up arms in the name of punishing Yang Guozhong. If you leave thirty thousand men to guard the pass and lead your elite forces back to execute Guozhong, that is the same plan by which the Han dynasty broke the Rebellion of the Seven Kingdoms. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 翰心許之，未發。

translations.literal: Han agreed in his heart but did not yet act.
translations.idiomatic: Han agreed in his heart but had not yet moved to carry it out.

sentences.zh: 有客泄其謀於國忠，國忠大懼，及奏曰：「兵法『安不忘危』，今潼關兵眾雖盛，而無後殿，萬一不利，京師得無恐乎！

translations.literal: A guest leaked the plan to Guozhong. Guozhong was greatly alarmed and memorialized: In warfare one must be secure and not forget danger. Though the forces at Tong Pass are strong, there is no reserve in the rear. If things go badly, will not the capital be thrown into fear?
translations.idiomatic: A guest betrayed the plan to Guozhong. Terrified, Guozhong memorialized the throne: "The art of war says that in safety one must not forget danger. Though the army at Tong Pass is large, there is no reserve behind it. If fortune turns, will the capital not be gripped by fear?

sentences.zh: 請選監牧小兒三千人訓練於苑中。」

translations.literal: Please select three thousand youths from the imperial stud farms and train them in the park.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that three thousand youths from the imperial stud farms be chosen and drilled in the palace park.

sentences.zh: 詔從之，遂遣劍南軍將李福、劉光庭分統焉。

translations.literal: The edict approved this, and Li Fu and Liu Guangting of the Jiannan army were sent to command them separately.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved, and Li Fu and Liu Guangting, generals of the Jiannan army, were dispatched to command them separately.

sentences.zh: 又奏召募一萬人，屯於灞上，令其腹心杜乾運將之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to recruit ten thousand men and station them at Bashang, putting his trusted follower Du Qianyun in command.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to recruit ten thousand men, station them at Bashang, and place them under his confidant Du Qianyun.

sentences.zh: 翰慮為所圖，乃上表請乾運兵隸於潼關，遂召乾運赴潼關計事，因斬之。

translations.literal: Han feared a plot against him and therefore submitted a memorial asking that Qianyun's troops be placed under Tong Pass. He then summoned Qianyun to Tong Pass to discuss affairs and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Han feared he was being plotted against and memorialized that Qianyun's troops be placed under Tong Pass command. He then summoned Qianyun to Tong Pass on the pretext of consultation and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 自是，翰心不自安。

translations.literal: From then on Han's heart was no longer at ease.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on Han's mind was never at rest.

sentences.zh: 又素有風疾，至是頗甚，軍中之務，不復躬親，委政於行軍司馬田良丘。

translations.literal: He had also long suffered from wind illness, which now grew severe. He no longer personally attended to military affairs and delegated authority to expedition chief of staff Tian Liangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He had long suffered from wind illness, and it now worsened considerably. He no longer handled military affairs in person and entrusted them to the expedition chief of staff, Tian Liangqiu.

sentences.zh: 良丘復不敢專斷，教令不一，頗無部伍。

translations.literal: Liangqiu in turn dared not decide alone, so orders were inconsistent and discipline broke down.
translations.idiomatic: Liangqiu, for his part, dared not decide matters on his own, orders conflicted, and the army lost all cohesion.

sentences.zh: 其將王思禮、李承光又爭長不葉，人無鬥志。

translations.literal: His generals Wang Sili and Li Chengguang also vied for precedence and would not cooperate; the men had no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: His generals Wang Sili and Li Chengguang also quarreled over precedence and would not work together, and the soldiers lost all fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 先是，翰數奏祿山雖竊河朔，而不得人心，請持重以弊之，彼自離心，因而翦滅之，可不傷兵擒茲寇矣。

translations.literal: Previously Han had repeatedly memorialized that though Lushan had seized Hebei, he had not won men's hearts, and asked to hold firm and wear the enemy down until they split apart, then cut them off and capture the bandits without heavy losses.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Han had repeatedly memorialized that although Lushan had seized Hebei, he had not won the people's hearts, and urged a patient defense to exhaust the rebels until they fell apart—then they could be destroyed and the bandits captured without great bloodshed.

sentences.zh: 賊將崔乾祐於陜郡潛鋒蓄銳，而覘者奏雲「賊殊無備」，上然之，命悉眾速討之。

translations.literal: The rebel general Cui Qianyou secretly sharpened his vanguard at Shaan commandery, but scouts reported that the rebels were wholly unprepared. The emperor believed this and ordered the whole force to attack swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Cui Qianyou secretly massed his best troops at Shaan commandery, yet scouts reported that the enemy was entirely unprepared. The emperor accepted this and ordered the full army to strike at once.

sentences.zh: 翰奏曰：「賊既始為AT逆，祿山久習用兵，必不肯無備，是陰計也。

translations.literal: Han memorialized: Since the rebels have taken up treason, and Lushan has long practiced warfare, he will surely not be unprepared—this is a hidden stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Han memorialized: "Now that the rebels have launched a treasonous revolt, Lushan, who has long been versed in war, will certainly not be caught unprepared. This report of slack defenses is a ruse.

sentences.zh: 且賊兵遠來，利在速戰。

translations.literal: Moreover, the rebel army has come from afar; its advantage lies in swift battle.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the rebel army has marched from far away; its advantage lies in forcing a quick battle.

sentences.zh: 今王師自戰其地，利在堅守，不利輕出；

translations.literal: Our army now fights on its own ground; its advantage lies in holding firm, not in sallying lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Our own forces fight on home ground; our advantage lies in holding the pass, not in sallying out lightly.

sentences.zh: 若輕出關，是入其算。

translations.literal: If we sally lightly from the pass, we walk into their calculation.
translations.idiomatic: If we leave the pass rashly, we fall straight into their trap.

sentences.zh: 乞更觀事勢。」

translations.literal: I beg to watch the situation further.
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to wait and observe how matters develop.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠恐其謀己，屢奏使出兵。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong feared Han's plot against him and repeatedly memorialized urging an advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong, fearing Han's designs against him, repeatedly memorialized urging the army to march out.

sentences.zh: 上久處太平，不練軍事，既為國忠眩惑，中使相繼督責。

translations.literal: The emperor had long lived in peace and was unskilled in military affairs. Deluded by Guozhong, he was pressed in succession by palace envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had lived so long in peace that he was unpracticed in war. Bewildered by Guozhong, he was driven on by one palace envoy after another.

sentences.zh: 翰不得已，引師出關。

translations.literal: Han had no choice but to lead his army out of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Han had no choice but to march his army out of the pass.

sentences.zh: 六月四日，次於靈寶縣之西原。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the sixth month he halted at Xiyuan in Lingbao county.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the sixth month he encamped at Xiyuan in Lingbao county.

sentences.zh: 八日，與賊交戰，官軍南迫險峭，北臨黃河；

translations.literal: On the eighth day he joined battle with the rebels. The imperial army was pressed on the south by steep cliffs and faced the Yellow River on the north.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day he engaged the rebels. The imperial army was hemmed in on the south by sheer cliffs and had the Yellow River at its back to the north.

sentences.zh: 崔乾祐以數千人先據險要。

translations.literal: Cui Qianyou with several thousand men had already seized the strategic heights.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qianyou had already taken the high ground with several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 翰及良丘浮船中流以觀進退，謂乾祐兵少，輕之，遂促將士令進，爭路擁塞，無復隊伍。

translations.literal: Han and Liangqiu floated a boat midstream to observe the advance and retreat. Thinking Qianyou's force small, they despised it and urged the soldiers forward. They scrambled for the road, crowding and blocking one another until there was no formation left.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Liangqiu took a boat into midstream to watch how the battle went. Believing Qianyou's force too small to matter, they treated it lightly and ordered the men forward. Soldiers jostled for the road until the ranks jammed together and all order vanished.

sentences.zh: 午後，東風急，乾祐以草車數十乘縱火焚之，煙焰亙天。

translations.literal: In the afternoon an east wind rose sharply. Qianyou set fire to several dozen carts of hay; smoke and flame filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the afternoon a fierce east wind sprang up. Qianyou torched several dozen hay carts, and smoke and flame blotted out the sky.

sentences.zh: 將士掩面，開目不得，因為兇徒所乘，王師自相排擠，墜於河。

translations.literal: The soldiers covered their faces and could not open their eyes. The rebels seized the moment; the imperial army trampled one another and fell into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers covered their faces and could not see. Seizing the moment, the rebels drove in; the imperial troops crushed one another and tumbled into the river.

sentences.zh: 其後者見前軍陷敗，悉潰，填委於河，死者數萬人，號叫之聲振天地，縛器械，以槍為楫，投北岸，十不存一二。

translations.literal: Those in the rear, seeing the vanguard collapse, all fled. The dead piled in the river by the tens of thousands. Their cries shook heaven and earth. Bound to their weapons, using spears as oars, they struck for the north bank; fewer than one in ten survived.
translations.idiomatic: Those behind, seeing the front ranks destroyed, broke and ran. Corpses choked the river by the tens of thousands, and their cries shook heaven and earth. Tangled with their weapons, using spears as paddles, they struggled toward the north bank—fewer than one in ten lived.

sentences.zh: 軍既敗，翰與數百騎馳而西歸，為火拔歸仁執降於賊。

translations.literal: After the defeat Han fled west with several hundred horsemen and was seized by Huoba Guiren, who surrendered him to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was broken, Han galloped west with several hundred horsemen, was seized by Huoba Guiren, and surrendered to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 祿山謂之曰：「汝常輕我，今日如何？」

translations.literal: Lushan said to him: You always looked down on me—how is it today?
translations.idiomatic: Lushan said to him, "You always despised me. How do you like your situation now?

sentences.zh: 翰懼，俯伏稱：「肉眼不識陛下，遂至於此。

translations.literal: Han, in fear, prostrated himself and said: These mortal eyes failed to recognize Your Majesty, and so I have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Han prostrated himself and said, "These mortal eyes failed to recognize Your Majesty, and so I have come to this pass.

sentences.zh: 陛下為撥亂主，今天下未平，李光弼在土門，來填在河南，魯炅在南陽，但留臣，臣以尺書招之，不日平矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is a lord who settles chaos. The realm is not yet pacified. Li Guangbi is at Tumen, Lai Tian at Henan, and Lu Kui at Nanyang. Keep me here, and with a single letter I can summon them—they will submit in no time and the realm will be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is a ruler who restores order amid chaos. The empire is not yet settled. Li Guangbi holds Tumen, Lai Tian holds Henan, and Lu Kui holds Nanyang. Keep me alive, and with a single letter I can win them over—the realm will be pacified in no time."

sentences.zh: 祿山大喜，遂偽署翰司空。

translations.literal: Lushan was greatly pleased and falsely appointed Han Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was delighted and falsely appointed Han Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 作書招光弼等，諸將報書皆讓翰不死節。

translations.literal: He wrote letters summoning Guangbi and the others. The generals replied, each reproaching Han for failing to die with honor.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote letters summoning Guangbi and the others. Every general wrote back to rebuke Han for failing to die rather than submit.

sentences.zh: 祿山知事不諧，遂閉翰於苑中，潛殺之。

translations.literal: Lushan saw that the plan would not succeed and therefore confined Han in the park and secretly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the scheme would not work, Lushan had Han imprisoned in the park and secretly put him to death.

sentences.zh: 翰之守潼關也，主天下兵權，肆誌報怨，誣奏戶部尚書安思順與祿山潛通，偽令人為祿山遺思順書，於關門擒之以獻。

translations.literal: While Han held Tong Pass he commanded the empire's military power and freely pursued grudges. He falsely memorialized that Minister of Revenue An Sishun was in secret communication with Lushan, forged a letter from Lushan to Sishun, and seized him at the pass gate to present to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: While Han held Tong Pass he wielded command over the empire's armies and freely settled old scores. He falsely accused Minister of Revenue An Sishun of secret dealings with Lushan, forged a letter purporting to be from Lushan to Sishun, and seized him at the pass to present to the throne.

sentences.zh: 其年三月，思順及弟太仆卿元貞坐誅，徙其家屬於嶺外，天下冤之。

translations.literal: In the third month of that year Sishun and his brother Yuanzhen, Grand Master of the Imperial Stud, were executed for the crime, and their families were exiled beyond the Ling Mountains. The realm considered it a gross injustice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of that year Sishun and his brother Yuanzhen, Grand Master of the Imperial Stud, were executed on the charge, and their families were banished beyond the Ling Mountains. All under heaven regarded it as a grievous wrong.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：大盜作梗，祿山亂常，詞雖欲誅國忠，誌則謀危社稷。

translations.literal: The historian says: When the great bandit raised rebellion, Lushan overturned the norm. Though his words claimed he sought to execute Guozhong, his intent was to endanger the state.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When the great outlaw rose in rebellion, Lushan overturned the moral order. Though his words called for Guozhong's death, his aim was to bring down the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 於時承平日久，金革道消，封常清、高仙芝相次率不教之兵，募市人之眾，以抗AT寇，失律喪師。

translations.literal: The realm had then enjoyed peace for so long that the way of war had faded. Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi in succession led untrained troops and masses of conscripted townsmen against the rebel bandits, violated military discipline, and lost their armies.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had lasted so long that the arts of war had fallen into neglect. Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi, one after the other, led undisciplined soldiers and crowds of hastily recruited townsfolk against the Jie rebel bandits, broke military law, and lost their armies.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰廢疾於家，起專兵柄，二十萬眾拒賊關門，軍中之務不親，委任又非其所。

translations.literal: Ge Shuhan, incapacitated at home, was raised to sole command of the army. Two hundred thousand men held the pass against the rebels, yet he did not personally attend to military affairs and entrusted them to men unsuited to the task.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Shuhan, broken by illness at home, was suddenly given sole command. Two hundred thousand men held the gate against the rebels, yet he no longer handled military affairs himself and delegated them to men ill suited for the role.

sentences.zh: 及遇羯賊，旋致敗亡，天子以之播遷，自身以之拘執，此皆命帥而不得其人也。

translations.literal: When they met the Jie rebels, defeat swiftly followed. The Son of Heaven was driven into exile, and Han himself was taken captive—all because the wrong men were chosen to lead armies.
translations.idiomatic: When they met the Jie rebels, ruin followed at once. The Son of Heaven was driven into exile, and Han himself was taken prisoner—all because the wrong commanders had been chosen.

sentences.zh: 《禮》曰：「大夫死眾。」

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says: A grand officer dies for his troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says, "A grand officer dies together with his men.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「謀人之軍師敗則死之。」

translations.literal: It also says: One who plots another's army—if the army is defeated, he dies for it.
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "He who serves as another's strategist—if the army is defeated, he dies for it."

sentences.zh: 翰受署賊庭，茍延視息，忠義之道，即可知也，豈不愧於顏杲卿乎！

translations.literal: Han accepted office in the rebel court and clung to life—his fidelity and righteousness may be judged from this. Is he not ashamed when compared with Yan Gaoqing!
translations.idiomatic: Han accepted a post in the rebel court and clung to life—what need is there to say of his loyalty and righteousness? How could he not blush before Yan Gaoqing!

sentences.zh: 抑又聞之，古之命將者，推轂而謂之曰：「閫外之事，將軍裁之。」

translations.literal: Yet it is also said that in antiquity, when appointing a general, the ruler would push the chariot forward and say: Matters beyond the gate are for the general to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one also hears that in antiquity, when a ruler appointed a general, he would push the chariot forward and say, "Matters beyond the gate are for the general alone to decide.

sentences.zh: 觀楊國忠之奏事，邊令誠之護戎，又掣肘於軍政者也，未可偏責三帥，不尤伊人。

translations.literal: Considering Yang Guozhong's memorials and Bian Lingcheng's protection of the frontier tribes, yet also his interference in military affairs, one cannot wholly blame the three commanders alone, nor should one condemn them without qualification.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Yang Guozhong's memorials and Bian Lingcheng's oversight of the frontier tribes—yet also his meddling in military affairs—and one cannot lay all blame on the three commanders alone, nor condemn them without reservation.

sentences.zh: 後之君子，得不深鑒！

translations.literal: Later gentlemen—should they not take this deeply to heart!
translations.idiomatic: Men of later ages—should they not take this deeply to heart!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：羯賊犯順，戎車啟行。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The Jie rebels violated the throne; war chariots rolled forth.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: The Jie rebels rose against the throne, and chariots of war set out.

sentences.zh: 委任失所，封、高敗亡。

translations.literal: Trust was misplaced; Feng and Gao were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Command was misplaced; Feng and Gao were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 虔劉圻甸，僭竊衣裳。

translations.literal: The heartland was ravaged; imperial robes were usurped.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland was laid waste; imperial vestments were stolen.

sentences.zh: 醜哉舒翰，不能死王。

translations.literal: Shameful was Shuhan—he could not die for his lord.
translations.idiomatic: Shame on Shuhan—he could not die for his sovereign.
